A repeated substring of length L implies a repeated prefix at every smaller length, so feasibility is monotone. Prefix hashes and powers compute the same paired signature for equal fixed-length windows. A matching signature is used only as a filter: every prior candidate is compared against the current slice before success is reported, so even a double-hash collision cannot create a false positive. Conversely, two equal windows necessarily share both signatures and the exact comparison accepts them. Testing every start permits overlapping occurrences, and upper-bound binary search therefore finishes at exactly the greatest feasible length, including zero when no non-empty repeat exists.
